text: In this book, an atlas {(U_α, φ_α)} on a topological manifold is called a smooth (C^∞) atlas precisely when which condition holds?
choices: Each chart map φ_α is a linear isomorphism of U_α onto ℝⁿ.
Every point of the manifold lies in exactly one chart U_α.
All transition maps φ_β ∘ φ_α⁻¹ are C^∞ diffeomorphisms of open subsets of ℝⁿ.
The manifold is compact and can be covered by a single global chart.
explanation: The book defines a smooth atlas as one whose transition maps φ_β ∘ φ_α⁻¹ are all C^∞ diffeomorphisms between open subsets of ℝⁿ; a smooth manifold then carries a maximal such atlas. Charts are homeomorphisms, not required to be linear, and they routinely overlap, which is exactly why the compatibility of the overlaps is what must be smooth. Requiring a single global chart would exclude S² and most manifolds of interest.
